markers.title: Bulk update button too short to tap
markers.body: The 'Bulk update' pill's text/icon box is only ~17dp tall, well under the 44dp minimum touch target. Increase vertical padding so the tappable area is at least 44dp, even if the visual pill stays compact.

markers.title: Filter chips (Room types, Rate plans, Channels) undersized
markers.body: Each filter chip's content is only ~16dp tall, far below the 44dp touch target minimum, and the three chips sit close together with little breathing room. Pad each chip to at least 44dp tall and add clearer gaps between them.

markers.title: 'Channel' column header mismatches its data
markers.body: The first column is labelled 'Channel' but every row underneath (Double Room, Standard Twin, Budget Studio…) is a room type or rate plan, not a distribution channel. Relabel the header to match the currently selected filter (e.g. 'Room type') or update it dynamically when the filter changes.

markers.title: Rate/inventory grid cells too small to tap precisely
markers.body: Each editable count/price cell (e.g. the '5' availability figures, '240'/'280' rates) is roughly 9–26dp wide and 17dp tall with no visible padding between adjacent cells. If these are meant to be tapped to edit, they're far under the 44×44dp guideline and risk mis-taps on a dense grid.

markers.title: Wide rate table has no horizontal-scroll affordance
markers.body: The date grid extends far beyond the 390dp viewport (14+ columns) but is abruptly cropped at the right edge with no fade, arrow, or scroll indicator hinting that more dates exist. Add a subtle edge fade or scroll hint so users know to swipe horizontally.

working_well: Weekend columns (SAT, SUN) get a subtle tinted background, making it easy to scan rest days at a glance.
Room types are grouped with a bold header row followed by their rate-plan sub-rows, giving the dense grid clear hierarchy.
The currently selected date (FRI 31) is highlighted with an underline and brand-orange color, standing out from the rest of the header row.
worth_considering: Consider freezing the first column (room type / rate plan names) so labels stay visible while scrolling horizontally through dates.
Light row dividers or alternating shading within the rate-plan sub-rows could make it easier to track a single row across many date columns.
The rate figures render in a fairly light gray — worth double-checking contrast against both the white and tinted weekend backgrounds.
